candidate.answerReason: There are \(4\times3=12\) ordered selections, and each unordered pair has exactly two orders, giving \(12/2=6\).

methods.label: Count ordered selections
methods.explanation: There are 12 ways when order matters. When order is disregarded, each combination corresponds to 2 permutations, so \(12/2=6\).
methods.levelReason: Uses elementary two-step counting and the distinction between ordered and unordered selections.

methods.label: List each pair once
methods.explanation: Label the four elements \(A,B,C,D\). Write each pair with its alphabetically earlier element first, so changing the order cannot repeat a selection. The complete list is \(AB,AC,AD,BC,BD,CD\), giving \(6\) selections.
methods.levelReason: Direct enumeration uses only the meaning of an unordered pair and requires fewer counting prerequisites.
